questions.question: Name 2 zoonoses acquired commonly or sporadically from petting zoos, livestock, and wild/small animals that cause each of the following clinical presentations.
questions.question_raw: Name 2 zoonoses that can be acquired commonly or sporadically from petting zoos, livestock, and wild/small animals that cause each of the following:
questions.model_answer:
a) Non-bloody diarrhea: (1) Salmonella (infected poultry/eggs, reptiles/turtles, chicks, rodents). (2) Giardia lamblia / Cryptosporidium (companion and farm animals; contaminated water).
b) Fever and lymphadenopathy: (1) Tularemia (Francisella tularensis, from rabbits/rodents) producing regional lymphadenopathy. (2) Plague (Yersinia pestis, flea-borne from rodents) with fever and buboes.
questions.beyond_mandell: Giardia and Cryptosporidium as petting-zoo/water diarrhea pathogens are standard IDSA/CDC teaching; this chapter names only Salmonella and E. coli for enteric zoonoses.

cohort_answer.text: Non-bloody diarrhea - Bacteria: Salmonella enteritidis (cats/dogs, turtles, reptiles, chicks, rodents), Yersinia enterocolitica (cats/dogs), Francisella tularensis (bunnies, rodents); Parasites: Giardia lamblia (beaver), Strongyloides (dog poop), E. histolytica (dogs), Toxocara cati/canis (cats/dogs), Cryptosporidium (cats/dogs). Fever and LAD: Bartonella (cats, body louse), Brucella (sheep/goat), Toxoplasmosis (cats), Lyme (tick bite), Yersinia pestis (flea), Tularemia (ticks, deer flies), Chagas (triatome bug), Monkeypox

questions.question: Name the vector (genus or common name) for each of the following diseases.
questions.question_raw: Name the vector of the disease (genus or common name).
questions.model_answer:
a) Dengue virus: Aedes mosquito (Aedes aegypti/albopictus).
b) Falciparum malaria: female Anopheles mosquito.
c) Trypanosoma cruzi: triatomine (reduviid) "kissing" bug.
d) Endemic (murine) typhus: rat flea (Xenopsylla cheopis).
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the mosquito vector of dengue is in this chapter (Table 317.1, p. 3815); Anopheles/malaria, triatomine/T. cruzi, and rat flea/murine typhus rest on standard Mandell/CDC knowledge.

cohort_answer.text: Dengue virus - Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus. Falciparum malaria - female Anopheles spp. Trypanosoma cruzi - Triatomine insect ('kissing' bug). Endemic Murine Typhus - Xenopsylla cheopis (Rat flea)
